newsitem.title: MEXICO: Cemex expects higher Mexico cement sales.
newsitem.headline: Cemex expects higher Mexico cement sales.

text.p: Mexican cement giant Cemex expects cement sales in Mexico to rise three to five percent this year compared to 1995, said Hector Medina, general manager of Cemex Mexico, Thursday.
Asked about growth in Mexico cement sales volume this year, Medina said:

"If these three last months which are left (of 1996) also show a better situation (than the last quarter of 1995)...we would be seeing a market which should be between three and five percent higher (compared to 1995)".
At the start of the year, Cemex had predicted 13 percent growth in Mexico cement sales. The adjustment in its estimate reflects its estimate for the growth in the overall size of the Mexican market.
For next year, Medina said: "We see a process of gradual recovery which probably in 1997 will mean that consumption will grow around six percent compared to 1996."
Medina also said Cemex's third quarter sales in Mexico had been better than those in the second quarter.
"At least in terms of volume, yes...prices are better, in volumes a bit better...at the operating level, it should be better", he said.
